test_title: PYST 70: SSC GD Constable 2022 - English (Held On : 09 Feb 2023 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

He had to __bite the bullet__ when the doctor told him that his injured foot had to be amputated.

options.text: To accept a difficult or unpleasant situation

solution: The correct answer is: **'To accept a difficult or unpleasant situation'**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The idiom **'bite the bullet' **is used in English when referring to facing a painful, difficult, or unpleasant situation courageously, almost as though preparing for the pain of a bullet wound. (कठिन परिस्थिति को स्वीकार करना) • **Example: **When his company was running out of funds, he decided to bite the bullet and let some employees go to save it from bankruptcy. • In the provided sentence, the phrase **'bite the bullet'** implies that the person has to accept the painful and unpleasant fact that his foot needs to be amputated. Therefore, the correct answer is- **'To accept a difficult or unpleasant situation'**. 36:Tc3d,
